boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all six frozen records in the Northern Virginia Campaign. Preserve per-engagement dates, including the adjoining August 22–25 and 25–27 intervals and the separate August 28 Thoroughfare Gap and August 28–30 Manassas records; VA024 is a frozen aggregate-operation record. The live NPS campaign heading does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.rationale: Changing daily populations over three days; no matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result remains Confederate victory. NPS says the Union left was crushed and the retreat precipitous; Ropes calls it a severe defeat but not a rout, with the army retiring in good order.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The sources disagree on the retreat's character; neither is adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 22,180 total (US 13,830; CS 8,350); the live NPS field reads 22179 total (US 13826; CS 8353;). Ropes cites the Confederate official list of casualties at Manassas Plains in August 1862 as 7,241 killed and wounded, and Jackson's reported total loss of 4,387 from the Rappahannock to the Potomac, disputes Lee's 7,000 unwounded prisoners, and says Federal losses can only be conjectured without returns.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Neither Ropes Confederate figure is bounded to this interval: the 7,241 is labelled only 'at Manassas Plains, in August, 1862' (killed and wounded), and Jackson's 4,387 runs from the Rappahannock to the Potomac, which Ropes would distribute over August 28–September 1.

open_questions: Original returns, despatch chains and casualty reconciliation remain deferred. Porter's conduct and orders, discussed at length by Ropes, are not adjudicated here.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Ropes is one retrospective history written from the Federal standpoint by a civilian author. Reports and despatches quoted inside Ropes are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
